page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native virtual server configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. This CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz across 2 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixed profile. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing and strong performance in text processing. However, multi-core and raw computational benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, fall into the bottom tier. Memory bandwidth is generally weak for read operations but reaches average levels for large-block write operations. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 single-threaded decompression, perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations show weaker throughput.

This server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. Because of the shared CPU allocation and lower multi-core benchmark results, it is best suited for lightweight database caching, text processing, basic web serving, or development environments where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute power.
